findings.summary: "Every N landings" is counted by comparing commit times with the sweep's local time, in whole seconds. The code already stores landing counts elsewhere, which avoids this.
findings.evidence: code_health.rs:392-427: `Landing.at` is the commit time (`%ct`) in epoch seconds, which the host sets for host merges. The plan counts `t > last.at.as_second()` and treats equal seconds as already seen, so a landing in the same second as the previous duty sweep is not counted. Fast fixture runs can do this. gh/landing.rs:972-984: after a squash merge, `resync_onto_merge` replaces the local landed commit with the host's merge commit, then calls `code_health_after_landing` again. steward.rs:105 already ran the hook at job finish, and the merge commit's time is later than that first sweep. So the second hook counts one new landing and runs code-health again. That contradicts the plan's claim that "the second hook for one landing runs nothing". The code already stores counts instead: `CodeHealthBaseline.landings` (code_health.rs:771, `total >= baseline.landings + REVIEW_EVERY`) and `ThroughputReview.landings` (throughput.rs:104). Fix: Record the landing total when a duty runs. For example, add an optional `landings: Option<u32>` to `HestiaCheckResult` with a serde default; criterion 7 already covers that record change. Count due as `landings(..).len() - recorded`. Add one test that lands a real job through the fixture with a host-style squash merge (a realistic-branch fixture, as in gh/after_merge_tests.rs `set_up`). It should show both hooks for one landing run code-health once.

findings.summary: The design-review duty has two schedules: the code reviews are actually queued on (the code-health baseline) and the one the duty table and status show.
findings.evidence: code_health.rs:766-778: `code_health_check`, which runs on every landing as the code-health duty, queues the design review whenever `total >= baseline.landings + REVIEW_EVERY` and writes a new baseline. The plan's design-review duty only reports the cached report, but its due point is counted from its own last sweep record. The two counters start at different times: the first baseline versus the duty's first run. So status can show design-review as "after 7 more landings" when the review was queued at the last landing, or the reverse. The table claims the sweep owns this cadence, but the baseline logic owns it. Fix: Derive the design-review duty's last run and next due from `CodeHealthBaseline` records: last run is the newest with `review_queued` (or the first baseline), next due is `baseline.landings + REVIEW_EVERY`. Its "run" is then the code-health pass it is already part of. Alternatively, list design review in the table as part of the code-health row, with its cadence stated from the baseline.
findings.location: Decision 4; Decision 7 (design-review EveryLandings(10)); Step 3 design-review arm

findings.summary: The 24-hour overdue rule for drain-start duties is a guess that the records could replace. It flags idle repositories and also changes what `athena hestia sweep` runs.
findings.evidence: The plan labels 24 h an estimate. Any repository not drained for a day shows the error-review and evidence-label duties as OVERDUE even though nothing was missed: a false positive by construction. Drain start always runs these duties (hestia.rs:2635 via drain.rs:3004), so after this change "past its cadence" can only mean a drain started and the duty failed. The records show that directly as an errored result newer than the last good one (the plan's `last_failed_at`). The 24 h rule also gates the Sweep occasion. Today, `hestia_sweep_with` (hestia.rs:2766-2771) runs backfill and derivation on every sweep. Under the plan they run only after 24 h, an unrequested behavior change; that is why the test at hestia.rs:5020 changes. Fix: Flag a drain-start duty as overdue when its newest attempt failed (`last_failed_at` newer than `last_run`), or when it has never run. Show next due as "at the next drain start". Drop the time limit, and keep `athena hestia sweep` running the drain-start duties every time, as it does now.

findings.summary: Partial sweep records written at drain start and at each landing become the "latest sweep", which changes what `athena hestia last` shows.
findings.evidence: `last_sweep` (hestia.rs:2834-2839) returns `HestiaSweep::latest` by `at`. `athena hestia last` reads it (crates/athena-cli/src/commands.rs:204; the plan's dependents list does not name this file). After every landing, the newest sweep would hold only the code-health result, so the last full sweep's branch and path findings no longer show. The field's doc comment says "Every check that was registered, in order" (throughput.rs:331); duty-only sweeps break that. The plan accepts this ("the check list in the report says so") without a test. Fix: Keep duty runs from shadowing the full sweep. Either make `last_sweep`/`hestia last` pick the newest sweep that ran the registered checks (or show both), or record duty runs in their own field or record. Add commands.rs:204 to the dependents list, with a test that a landing pass does not hide the previous full sweep's findings.
findings.location: Decision 1; Dependents entry for the `athena.hestia-sweep/1` record shape

findings.summary: A drain test the change breaks is missing from the dependents list: drain.rs:5909 asserts that a drain commits nothing.
findings.evidence: crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs:5905-5909 runs `drain::drain(&steps, work_everything(), &ui)` with `real_steps_with`, then asserts `fx.head() == head` ("nothing was read or run"). `drain_with` calls `steps.review_passes()` at every drain start (drain.rs:3004), and `RealSteps::review_passes` calls `Athena::review_passes` (drain.rs:4354). Under the plan, the DrainStart duties are always due at that occasion and commit a sweep record, so the head moves and this test fails. The plan names only drain.rs:4622. Fix: Add drain.rs:5909 to the dependents list and Step 9. Change its assertion to allow exactly one duty sweep record and no other record. Grep the cli tests for other drains using `real_steps_with` that check head or record counts, and list each one.

findings.summary: Every drain and every landing now writes a commit to the records branch, even when nothing changed.
findings.evidence: The second-drain test (drain.rs:4612-4622) states as a property that "a second drain ... writes nothing". The plan gives that up for every drain and every landing, which is two commits per landing in the host-merge flow (steward.rs:105 and gh/landing.rs:984). Fix: If last runs are stored as counts (finding 1) and drain-start failures carry the overdue signal (finding 3), commit a drain-start duty record only when a duty's outcome changed or it errored. Otherwise accept the cost explicitly and state it in the CHANGELOG entry.
findings.location: Risks, first entry; Decision 9 rejected alternative

summary: The plan covers every acceptance criterion. Its test seams exist: `athena_in`, `commit_sweep`, `last_sweep`, `run_sweep`, `code_health_after_landing`, `landings`, `keep_rule` and `REVIEW_EVERY` are all where it says. `HestiaSweep::validate` accepts a sweep with no checks, so committing a sweep where no duty ran works. I found five major problems, so the verdict is revise. (1) "Every N landings" is counted by comparing commit times with the sweep's local `at`, in whole seconds. The codebase's own pattern is to store a landing count (`CodeHealthBaseline.landings`, `ThroughputReview.landings`). Comparing times gives wrong answers on same-second landings and clock skew, and it breaks the plan's own claim that the second landing hook runs nothing: when the host squash-merges, the replacement commit has a later commit time than the first hook's sweep. (2) The design-review duty only reports a review that `code_health_check` queues on its own baseline counter. Its "every 10 landings" row and its status "next due" therefore follow a second counter that can drift from when reviews are really queued. (3) The 24-hour limit for drain-start duties is a guess that flags any idle repository as overdue. It also stops `athena hestia sweep` from running the backfill and evidence-label passes it runs today. (4) Drain and landing passes would write partial sweep records. These become the "latest sweep" that `athena hestia last` shows, which hides the full sweep's findings and contradicts the documented meaning of `HestiaSweep.checks`. (5) A drain test the change breaks, crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs:5909, is missing from the dependents list. Athena's three scope findings are justified as minor; the plan explains why each extra file is needed.
